correctness.rationale: Exact conditional-colouring expectation and variance give the proposed Gram block matrix. Frequency orthogonality and orthogonal leaf-contrast decomposition give all eigenvalues including singular boundaries. Trace and determinant establish strict sharp extrema and monotonicity, and their asymptotics yield the s^2 coefficient. Independent finite numerical checker passed 228 assertion groups; this verifies examples only, not the infinite theorem.

originality.rationale: Compared implications rather than titles: primary H-colouring and corona literature fixes related objects but does not identify all-core colouring-character Gram spectra, rank persistence, strict degradation, or the sharp s-squared coefficient. Earlier same-category fixed-graph Fourier claims do not imply the universal pendant transfer. Residual possibility of a broader unlocated covariance theorem is retained.
residual_risks: An unlocated published general Potts two-point covariance / conditional-variance theorem may already imply the transfer in a different normalization.
A standard spectral-corona matrix identity resembles the block algebra, although its graph-adjacency eigenvalues do not determine the present colour-sampling Gram spectrum.
Only a bounded set of older primary sources was materially inspected; complete historical uniqueness is not established.

value.rationale: The theorem settles a graph-independent reconstruction-stability question under a natural ubiquitous graph operation, including exact preservation of dependencies, a strict conditioning penalty, and a sharp universal quadratic growth law whose leading factor ignores the least original eigenvalue. A complete q-color threshold for decorated cliques is a nontrivial natural specialization. It is not a free restatement of an adjacency corona spectrum or an arbitrary finite computation.
